	2027 Oscar Predictions: ‘The Odyssey’ Hits the Campaign Trail, ‘You Can See Everything’ Loses DGA Eligibility and Zendaya Makes Her Move
	



			
			
	
						

									 Director Christopher Nolan on the set of his film 'The Odyssey,'  Melinda Sue Gordon
	
					


							
		

	Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change based on buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.



	

					YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING, Elizabeth Holmes (back left), director Nathan Fielder (right), on set, 2026. © A24/Courtesy Everett Collection
									Courtesy Everett Collection
	




	2027 Academy Awards Predictions Commentary All Categories (Updated: Nov. 5, 2026): It’s November, the Oscar race is finding its rhythm and the campaigns are beginning to show their hands.

	Universal Pictures’ official Oscar campaign for Christopher Nolan’s epic kicks off in earnest the week of Nov. 9, with a run of screenings and Q & As that puts Nolan, producer Emma Thomas and star Matt Damon in front of voters nearly every night for two weeks.

	Variety confirmed that Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s “You Can See Everything” will not be in the running for the Directors Guild of America Awards’ top prize this season.

	Zendaya will campaign for Oscar consideration in the lead actress category for her role as Chani in “Dune: Part Three,” the final chapter of Denis Villeneuve’s sci-fi epic. In the same vein, Mubi will campaign Sandra Hüller and co-star Hanns Zischler in the supporting categories at the Oscars and across the awards circuit for “Rose.”

	The final drips of Golden Globe submissions were revealed, with Jordan Firstman’s “Club Kid,” his feature debut as writer, director and star, submitted in the drama categories. Amazon MGM Studios will be juggling two contenders in musical or comedy: Phil Lord and Chris Miller’s “Project Hail Mary,” starring Ryan Gosling and Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky,” starring Anthony Ippolito.

	On the Oscar chart front, Nolan’s “The Odyssey” still leads the fray with 14 projected noms, which would tie for the second-most of all time alongside “All About Eve,” “Titanic” and “La La Land,” behind the record-setting 16 earned by “Sinners” last year, a mark “The Odyssey” could still tie or break.

	The films still waiting in the wings include Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three,” David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,” Anthony and Joe Russo’s “Avengers: Doomsday” and Robert Eggers’ “Werwulf,” each of which can or will, shake up a few categories in its own right.

	This week’s updates are below.

	The Governors Awards, which will hand out honorary Oscars to Glenn Close and Ridley Scott, will take place Sunday, Nov. 15. Preliminary voting for the Oscar shortlists in 12 categories runs Dec. 7-11, with the shortlist announcement to follow Tuesday, Dec. 15. Following the close of the eligibility period on Dec. 31, 2026, nominations voting will run Jan. 11-15, 2027. The Academy will announce the official Oscar nominations on Thursday, Jan. 21, 2027. The 99th Oscars will take place Sunday, March 14, 2027 and Conan O’Brien will host. The ceremony airs live at 7 p.m. ET on ABC and in more than 200 territories worldwide from the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood.

title: Kimmarie Johnson, ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ Actress and Miss USA Contestant, Dies at 50
description: Kimmarie Johnson, a model and actress who appeared in “Beverly Hills, 90210,” “Dude, Where’s My Car?” and more, died Wednesday, Nov. 4, after suffe
body:
Kimmarie Johnson, a model and actress who appeared in “Beverly Hills, 90210,” “Dude, Where’s My Car?” and more, died Wednesday, Nov. 4, after suffering a “heart event” at her Los Angeles home on Oct. 27. She was 50.

	Johnson had been taken to Cedars-Sinai Hospital and was diagnosed with a “heart aneurysm condition.” “She radiated a light so strong and bright,” her niece Rhonda Scott said in a statement to People. “People who came in contact with her felt nothing but positive energy. We will miss her tremendously and will continue to honor her life forever.”
	

	Johnson was also a model who won the title of Miss Pennsylvania and competed in the Miss USA beauty pageant in 1993. She was born on April 8, 1976, in Pittsburgh, Penn. She studied elementary education and child psychology at California University of Pennsylvania before moving to New York City and pursuing a career in modeling. After modeling for brands like Vidal Sassoon, Oscar de la Renta and United Colors of Benetton, she won Miss Pennsylvania without any prior pageant experience. Johnson then finished in the top five of the Miss USA 1993 competition.

	In 1996, she moved to Los Angeles to continue modeling and start her acting career. She booked her first  major TV part on an episode of “Beverly Hills, 90210” and her first movie role in the 2000 comedy “Dude, Where’s My Car?” as “Alien Jumpsuit Chick #5.” She also appeared in “Carman: The Champion,” “The Summer of Massacre,” “VIP,” “Wanda at Large” and more.

	In 2011, Johnson founded the skin care and beauty brand SkinGlow by Kimmarie.

title: Perspective Films Reveals Inaugural Documentary Film Slate (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Perspective Films, a new documentary co-production initiative led by independent producer Jess Devaney, has unveiled its inaugural slate of films,
body:
Perspective Films, a new documentary co-production initiative led by independent producer Jess Devaney, has unveiled its inaugural slate of films, Variety can report exclusively. The subjects of Perspective’s first five documentaries include the clash between federal immigration enforcement and the citizens of Minneapolis, the war in Gaza and the invention of C-SPAN. 

	“Every story on this slate is about who gets to shape history — a concert that sparked a movement, a network that threw open the halls of power to the public and residents documenting state violence as it unfolds,” Devaney said. “These films bring together Oscar-winning directors, veteran producers, and a journalist reporting from inside a war zone. They are collaborators of extraordinary talent and courage, and we’re proud to partner on their visionary films.”
	

	Devaney, Perspective’s narrative strategist and the founder of Multitude Films, joined the label in May. Her previous works include “Life After,” “Pray Away” and “Power” for Netflix, the Emmy-winning “Lowndes County and the Road to Black Power” and HBO’s “How We Get Free.”

	Perspective Films was built from the Perspective Fund’s Documentary Film Support program, which, under the leadership of program officer Andrew Catauro, offers grant funding for nonfiction projects. Selected titles receive up to $375,000 toward development, filming, post-production or distribution. Perspective Films also offers guidance at every step of the filmmaking process from conception to release.   

	See Perspective Film’s initial slate below. 
	

	“THEY’RE HERE,” which premiered at the Venice and New York Film Festivals this year, is a documentary that unfolds like a horror film that follows Edén Villa (a pseudonym) and anonymous Minneapolis residents as they evade and resist the paramilitary occupation of their city. Told in the tradition of dystopian cinema, “THEY’RE HERE” is set in a winter landscape where masked agents abduct children, residents travel in trunks, shackled prisoners are loaded onto airplanes within eyesight of vacationers and bicyclists track the movements of an invading force. Directed by Academy Award-winning filmmaker Laura Poitras and Minneapolis-based filmmaker Rachel Lauren Mueller. Produced by Rachel Lauren Mueller, Laura Poitras, Yoni Golijov. Screening at film festivals.

	“THE PEOPLE’S NETWORK,” traces C-SPAN’s evolution of almost five decades from a bold experiment into an essential civic institution. After revolutionizing access to government in the age of cable, C-SPAN now faces a new era and a renewed question: how to best serve the public at a time when America needs it the most? Directed by Alyse Shorland; produced by Darcy McKinnon and Sara Archambault. In Production.

	“UNTITLED GAZA DOCUMENTARY,” details embargoed until launch. Directed by anonymous. Produced, written and edited by Rabab Haj Yahya; produced by Ayah Selene and Munir Atalla. In post-production.

	“FARM AID,” tells the story of Willie Nelson, Neil Young and John Mellencamp organizing what they thought would be a one-time benefit concert for small family farmers in 1985. Forty years later, the crisis has reached another breaking point and the movement that refused to let rural America disappear is still fighting. Directed by Kathlyn Horan; produced by Academy Award nominees Julie Goldman and Christopher Clements and Emmy winner J. Daniel Torres. In production.

	“UNTITLED POLICING DOCUMENTARY” explores media and cultural portrayals of policing. Directed by Academy Award-nominated director Geeta Gandbhir; produced by Academy Award-nominated producer Alisa Payne. In development.

title: Wyatt Russell’s Monsterverse Series at Apple TV Adds Tim Robbins, Giancarlo Esposito
description:
Tim Robbins and Giancarlo Esposito are set for guest star roles in the new Monsterverse series in the works at Apple TV, Variety has learned. 

	Ro
body:
Tim Robbins and Giancarlo Esposito are set for guest star roles in the new Monsterverse series in the works at Apple TV, Variety has learned. 

	Robbins and Esposito will appear opposite series lead Wyatt Russell and previously announced cast members Millie Brady, Pilou Asbaek, Corey Stoll, Ralph Ineson, Nyasha Hatendi, Connie Nielsen and Stana Katic.

	The series will again see Russell play a young Col. Lee Shaw, whom he plays in “Monarch: Legacy of Monsters.” The logline for the spinoff states that Shaw is “an American operative who in 1984 went on a secret mission behind enemy lines in an attempt to stop the Soviets from unleashing a horrific new Titan big enough to destroy the U.S. and turn the tide of the Cold War.” 
	

	Further character details are being kept under wraps. 

	This will be the second Apple series for Robbins, who also stars in the streamer’s popular series “Silo.” He has also been in shows like “The Brink,” “Here and Now,” and “Castle Rock.” In film, Robbins won an Academy Award for his work in the film “Mystic River,” while he also received a nod for best director for the film “Dead Man Walking.” He known for starring in features like “The Player,” “The Shawshank Redemption,” and “Bull Durham.” 

	Esposito is known for TV roles in shows like “Breaking Bad” and “Better Call Saul,” as well as “The Gentlemen,” “The Boys,” “The Mandalorian,” and “Godfather of Harlem.” In film, he is known for collaborating with Spike Lee on features including “Do the Right Thing,” “School Daze,” “Mo’ Better Blues,” and “Jungle Fever.” 

	Robbins is repped by CAA and Anonymous Content. Esposito is repped by UTA, MGMT Entertainment, Jackoway Austen Tyerman, and The Initiative Group. 
	

	The untitled Monsterverse series is executive produced by Joby Harold and Tory Tunnell for Safehouse Pictures. Harold is also showrunning and developing multiple projects in the Legendary Monsterverse. Russell also executive produces along with Andy Goddard, Kyle Bradstreet, Jim Skotchdopole, Max Borenstein, Chris Black, and Alex Boden. JD Dillard will serve as director and executive producer. Hiro Matsuoka and Takemasa Arita executive produce on behalf of Toho Co., Ltd., the owner of the Godzilla character.

	It was recently reported that “Monarach” is eyeing a major creative reboot should it go to a third season, which would mean a new writing team and showrunner would take over the franchise.

title: Netflix Names Mattel Executive Roberto Stanichi as VP of Consumer Products and Experiences
description: Netflix has hired Roberto Stanichi as its vice president of consumer products and experiences, poaching him away from his role as Mattel’s chief ma
body:
Netflix has hired Roberto Stanichi as its vice president of consumer products and experiences, poaching him away from his role as Mattel’s chief marketing and brand officer.

	At Netflix, Stanichi will be tasked with overseeing Netflix’s global consumer products and licensing business and its global experiences division, including its newer Netflix House activations. He will report to Marian Lee, Netflix’s chief marketing officer.


	“Roberto has spent his career turning iconic characters and stories into global brands that resonate across generations,” Lee said in a statement. “As we continue to build on the incredible fandom around Netflix’s stories and characters, his experience will be invaluable in shaping how those connections extend beyond the screen and into fans’ everyday lives.”
	

	Stanichi has some familiarity with Netflix, having worked with the streamer and Hasbro on a toy partnership for animated smash movie “KPop Demon Hunters.” He spent nearly 20 years at Mattel, working on brands including Barbie, Hot Wheels, Fisher-Price and American Girl. A Brazil native, Stanichi also held leadership roles at Spin Master and PepsiCo.

	Stanichi fills the role left vacant after Josh Simon left Netflix as head of consumer products in August 2025 to join Funko as CEO. His hiring also follows Greg Lombardo’s exit last month as Netflix VP of creative and production for global experiences.

	Mattel confirmed Stanichi’s exit and said he is stepping down from the company effective Nov. 10. Also Thursday, Mattel announced that Steve Totzke, formerly president and chief commercial officer, was stepping into a new role as president and COO. Totzke is taking an expanded role overseeing marketing and brand (which was Stanichi’s area), as well as sales and consumer products.
	

	Stanichi said in a statement provided by Netflix: “Few companies in the world understand the emotional power of storytelling and fandom like Netflix. It is an incredible privilege to join Marian and this extraordinary team to help expand that fandom into physical worlds, products, and experiences. Netflix’s culture of bold innovation and creative ambition is legendary, and I’m excited to dive in to create impactful touchpoints that bring our fans closer to the stories they love.”

	Netflix launched its first major consumer product line with Season 1 of “Stranger Things,” expanding it across its catalog to franchises like “Bridgerton” and “KPop Demon Hunters.” It has also launched more than 50 live experience formats, including Netflix House venues in Philadelphia and Dallas. Its third location, on the Las Vegas Strip, is slated to open next year.

	Stanichi’s hiring comes just weeks after Netflix laid off 6% of its staff, about 1,000 staffers. Those let go include its chief content officer, Bela Bajaria, and head of film Dan Lin. Veteran Hollywood executive Peter Rice joined the company as chief content officer late last month.

schema.headline: Netflix Names Mattel Executive Roberto Stanichi as VP of Consumer Products and Experiences

title: Fox Entertainment Studios Signs First-Look Deal With Lisa Hamilton Daly and Alysia Cotter Thomas’ Cottage Industry Entertainment
description: Fox Entertainment Studios has sealed a first-look development and producing deal with Cottage Industry Entertainment, the shingle launched by execu
body:
Fox Entertainment Studios has sealed a first-look development and producing deal with Cottage Industry Entertainment, the shingle launched by executives Lisa Hamilton Daly and Alysia Cotter Thomas. Among the slate of scripted television series and feature films in the works is “The Whittiers,” based on the Danielle Steel novel, which Fox has optioned to adapt for TV.

	Besides “The Whittiers,” other TV projects Fox Entertainment Studios is developing with Cottage Industry include a one-hour family drama from writer Jordanna Fraiberg (“The Dead Girls Detective Agency”); an adaptation of the Lindsay MacMillan novel “Summer on Lilac Island,” with Delondra Mesa (“Z Nation”) attached to write; and the comedy “Mom’s Place,” from Angela Kinsey (“The Office”) and Audrey Wauchope (“Crazy Ex-Girlfriend”).
	

	In film, Cottage Industry is working with Fox Entertainment Studios on the hockey-themed romantic comedy “It All Comes Down to This,” from screenwriters Sam Sklaver and Elizabeth Peterson; “The View from Lake Como,” based on the novel by Adriana Trigiani, who is also adapting it; and an adaptation of author Cynthia Hand’s “The Afterlife of Holly Chase” by Ali Laventhol and Tawnya Bhattacharya.

	Hamilton Daly and Cotter Thomas founded Cottage Industry Entertainment to focus on “emotionally engaging, female-driven storytelling spanning romantic comedies, family dramas, mysteries, thrillers and other broadly appealing genres.”

	“Lisa and Alysia bring a terrific combination of creative instincts, industry experience and a real understanding of what connects with audiences,” said Fox Entertainment Studios head of scripted Hannah Pillemer in a statement. “Lisa has helped build some of television’s most successful and enduring female-driven series, while Alysia has spent her career developing films and championing filmmakers, storytellers and other outstanding creative voices. Together, they’ve created a company with a clear point of view, a strong commercial sensibility and a growing slate of projects that we’re pleased to welcome to Fox.”
	

	Hamilton Daly was previously executive vice president of programming at Hallmark Media, overseeing fare such as “The Way Home,” “When Calls the Heart,” “Holiday Touchdown: A Chiefs Love Story,” “Mistletoe Murders” and “Ripple.” She was also director of original series at Netflix and also spent time at Lifetime and A+E Films. Cotter Thomas was most recently a literary agent at Paradigm, packaging projects including Ross Evan’s spec script “How to Save a Marriage” to Sony Pictures. Earlier, she held a stint at Warner Bros., including as part of the team that developed the “Batman” franchise with Christopher Nolan. She was also a VP at Legendary Entertainment and later served as VP of creative affairs at Working Title in London.

	“Fox Entertainment Studios has been a tremendous partner in helping us build Cottage Industry and bring our creative vision to life,” Hamilton Daly and Cotter Thomas said in a joint statement. “We share a belief in stories that entertain, move people and keep audiences coming back, whether that’s a compelling family drama, a smart romantic comedy or a suspenseful thriller. Hannah and her team understand both the creative and business sides of what we’re building, and we’re looking forward to continuing to develop projects together across television and film.”

title: ‘Hyena,’ Thriller Exec Produced by David Lynch, to Star Kiernan Shipka, D’Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai, Edgar Ramírez and Rosemarie DeWitt
description: One of the final film projects of the late Hollywood icon David Lynch is heading to the American Film Market with a fresh cast and a production sta
body:
One of the final film projects of the late Hollywood icon David Lynch is heading to the American Film Market with a fresh cast and a production start date. 

	The psychological thriller “Hyena,” which Lynch exec produced, will star Kiernan Shipka, D’Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai, Edgar Ramírez, Rosemarie DeWitt. Scott Coffey, who starred in Lynch’s “Mullholland Drive,” will direct, while Oscar-nominated producer David Lancaster (“Whiplash”) also exec produces. 
	

	Coffey directs from a screenplay he co-wrote with novelist Blair Mastbaum. Production is slated to begin in Spokane, Washington early next year.

	“Hyena” follows Genevieve (Shipka), who brings her enigmatic new boyfriend Alexei (Woon-A-Tai) home to meet her seemingly idyllic family. Their attempts to welcome him begin to fracture as Alexei turns his attention toward the family, working his way into them and exposing long-buried secrets, desires and hypocrisies — until Genevieve is the only one left willing to see him clearly, and saving what remains of her family demands an unspeakable sacrifice.

	The film is among the last credits for Lynch, the iconic filmmaker who died in January 2025. Coffey appeared as Wilkins in Mulholland Drive, and following this collaboration, Lynch became a mentor to Coffey and was closely involved in the early development of “Hyena.”

	“Hyena is a very personal film. I’ve always believed the most unsettling horror isn’t supernatural — it’s the moment grief and love turn feral, when we stop pretending we aren’t wild,” said Coffey, whose previous features include “Ellie Parker” and “Adult World.” “Kiernan Shipka, D’Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai, Edgar Ramírez, and Rosemarie DeWitt will bring extraordinary depth, intelligence, and vulnerability to the movie.”
	

	Shipka’s credits include Osgood Perkins’ “Longlegs,” Gia Coppola’s “The Last Showgirl,” Macon Blair’s “Idiots,” HBO’s smash hit “Industry” and AMC’s “Mad Men.” Woon-A-Tai is known for his performance in FX’s “Reservation Dogs.” He was most recently seen in Andrew Haigh’s “A Long Winter,” Darren Aronofsky’s “Caught Stealing” and Alex Garland’s “Warfare.” Ramírez was recently be seen in Jacques Audiard’s Oscar-winning “Emilia Pérez” and Eli Roth’s “Borderlands.” Next up, he’ll headline season two of HBO’s acclaimed series “Task.” Known for “Rachel Getting Married” and “La La Land,” DeWitt recently starred in “Smile 2,” can currently be seen in the Netflix crime drama “Untamed” opposite Erica Bana, and starred in Cannes entry “Diamond” alongside Andy Garcia, Brendan Fraser, Bill Murray & Dustin Hoffman.

	Upgrade and WME Independent are handling sales on Hyena and will introduce the project to buyers at the upcoming fall market. David Lancaster (Whiplash, Nightcrawler) will produce alongside Jeff Elliott (Canary Black).

	“Hyena” was previously packaged with Archie Madekwe and Havana Rose Liu to star, with a 2025 shoot date.

schema.headline: ‘Hyena,’ Thriller Exec Produced by David Lynch, to Star Kiernan Shipka, D’Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai, Edgar Ramírez and Rosemarie DeWitt

title: Nithya Raman Wins L.A. Mayor’s Race as Karen Bass Concedes
description:
Nithya Raman will be the next mayor of Los Angeles,  as incumbent Karen Bass conceded defeat after a hard-fought campaign.

	In a video, Raman than
body:
Nithya Raman will be the next mayor of Los Angeles,  as incumbent Karen Bass conceded defeat after a hard-fought campaign.

	In a video, Raman thanked Bass for her service and vowed to provide a city government that is “actually capable of delivering on its promises.” She cited priorities such as affordable housing, parks and public transit.

	“I love this city, and I love its people, and I cannot wait to get started on building a better future together with all of you,” Raman said. “Thank you so much, Los Angeles.”
	

	Bass conceded on Thursday morning as Raman’s lead continued to grow.

	“While this is not the outcome we hoped for, the people of Los Angeles have spoken,” Bass said in a statement. “I have called Councilmember Nithya Raman to congratulate her on her victory, and I have committed to ensuring a smooth and seamless transition. Moving this city forward is what Los Angeles needs from all of us.”

	Raman surprised the City Hall establishment by entering the race at the last minute in February, and appeared likely to finish third behind reality star Spencer Pratt through much of the primary. But she was able to rally enough voters fed up with Bass and open to a Democratic alternative.

	Early tallies on election night saw Bass with a slender lead over Raman — but not nearly enough of a margin to account for Raman’s strength with late-arriving ballots, which skew toward young voters and renters. Raman took the lead late on election night and the margin has continued to grow.

	As of the update on Thursday morning, Raman held a 4.2% lead over Bass — with many thousands of ballots still to count.
	

	Bass sought to focus on public safety, warning that Raman had opposed police funding and was against anti-camping zones. Raman, meanwhile, argued that the city needed fresh leadership that was not captive to relationships at City Hall.

	Raman led in several polls taken during the fall. But a Berkeley IGS/L.A. Times poll on Oct. 28 showed the two candidates tied, with both earning 40% of voters’ support. 

	On Tuesday night, shortly after 11 p.m., Raman addressed her supporters at her election-night event in the plaza of L.A.’s Greek Theatre. “I’m very hopeful,” she told the crowd. 

	Raman first joined the Los Angeles City Council in 2020, becoming the first Asian-American woman and the first South Asian ever to serve. She was re-elected for a second term in 2024. Raman holds degrees from Harvard and MIT, and worked as an urban planner before turning her focus to politics. She also served as the co-chair of the Silver Lake Neighborhood Council Homelessness Committee and co-founded the SELAH Neighborhood Homeless Coalition.

	During her campaign, Raman was particularly popular among the Hollywood set, earning endorsements and contributions from Tina Fey, Adam Scott, Mindy Kaling, Mike Schur, Colin Jost, Nicholas Stoller, Cord Jefferson, David Mandel, and others. 

	Bass, who has served as Los Angeles’ mayor since 2022, faced considerable challenges in winning back voters who were upset about homelessness, civic disorder and her handling of the 2025 Palisades fire.

title: Dear Oscars: Don’t Let Laika and ‘Wildwood’ Fail. There Is No Backup Stop-Motion Studio Waiting in the Wings
description: Travis Knight built 231 puppets and 136 sets to make “Wildwood.” Over the Laika film’s opening three-day weekend, audiences at 2,942 theaters bough
body:
Travis Knight built 231 puppets and 136 sets to make “Wildwood.” Over the Laika film’s opening three-day weekend, audiences at 2,942 theaters bought enough tickets to cover roughly a 10th of what the film reportedly cost.

	“Wildwood” opened to $12.2 million, behind DC’s “Clayface” and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary nobody can stop talking about. It earned an A CinemaScore and a 99% Fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes. This past weekend, it came in at No. 3 with another $7.5 million, bringing its grand total to $25 million domestically and $35 million globally.
	

	And it did all that with a PG-13 rating, a 131-minute run time and a studio that has earned five Oscar nods for animated feature in five tries. Against a reported $100 million budget, this doesn’t feel like a win. It feels like an alarm sounding for the health of the stop-motion animation community.

	Stop-motion is more expensive than traditional animation because every character is a physical puppet, every set is built by hand and animators nudge each figure a fraction of an inch and photograph it dozens of times for a single second of film.

	Stop-motion is a labor force, and that labor force is shrinking. Tippett Studio, the shop that helped teach Hollywood how to move from puppets to pixels, has announced that it is closing. Laika is now the only American studio still investing nine figures in the art form, and it exists largely because Phil Knight’s Nike fortune has absorbed losses that would have shuttered almost any other operation. Laika’s previous film, “Missing Link,” grossed $17 million domestically in 2019. It spent seven years making the follow-up.
	

	Travis Knight is Phil Knight’s son and Laika’s CEO. Nepotism, by its usual definition, can buy access. But the Knights have used their resources to pursue stop motion at a time when other shops are turning off the lights. That’s using your powers for good.

	Travis Knight knows what’s at stake. “We’ve tried to keep the art form alive for over 20 years now,” he told Variety after a “Wildwood” screening at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival. He added, “Art needs advocacy. It needs champions. It wears its humanity openly. It deserves to stay alive.”

	This is where the Academy could make a difference. The Academy has long treated animation as a separate lane, even as the medium has produced some of cinema’s most ambitious and emotionally sophisticated work. Only three animated films have been nominated for best picture; the most recent, “Toy Story 3,” arrived 15 years ago.

	A best picture nomination would put Laika on the industry’s biggest stage in a news cycle drowning in AI. Academy voters have a chance to affirm that physical labor and the human touch still matters.

	One Academy member says of “Wildwood”: “I was transported. It reminded me of the movies my children would watch in the ’80s, when movies believed children were smart enough to understand the difficult moments of life.”

	That is the perfect argument for “Wildwood” and for Laika. Hollywood is built on imagination and should be wary of letting one of its most distinctive forms of filmmaking become extinct.

	Not every movie needs to be made the way “Wildwood” was. But if Hollywood wants to keep that possibility alive, somebody has to buy a ticket and somebody has to vote.

title: HBO’s ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 Ratings: Most-Watched Premiere Yet
description: Things are still looking gilded for HBO’s “The Gilded Age.” The series returned on Nov. 1 to its most-watched season premiere yet, averaging nearly
body:
Things are still looking gilded for HBO’s “The Gilded Age.” The series returned on Nov. 1 to its most-watched season premiere yet, averaging nearly 4 million viewers across platforms, according to the cabler/streamer. 

	In the first three days of availability, “The Gilded Age” scored just under 4 million viewers across linear and HBO Max, the platform announced. That’s up 25% from last season’s premiere, which averaged 3.2 million. HBO noted that once a longer tail of delayed multiplatform viewership was tallied up, “The Gilded Age” Season 3 averaged 8.8 million viewers per episode.
	

	“The Gilded Age” Season 4 airs Sunday nights at 9 p.m. ET on HBO and streams on HBO Max. Here’s the Season 4 logline: “Bertha Russell changed Society at a cost. Now, her family must reckon with the consequences as Agnes van Rhijn seizes an opportunity to regain her position. Meanwhile, Marian forges a new path for herself and Peggy works to be accepted by her future in-laws. In this new era, you must be careful what you wish for.”

	The Season 4 cast includes Carrie Coon, Christine Baranski, Cynthia Nixon, Morgan Spector, Louisa Jacobson, Denée Benton, Taissa Farmiga, Harry Richardson, Blake Ritson, Ben Ahlers, Ashlie Atkinson, Dylan Baker, Kelley Curran, Jordan Donica, Jessica Frances Dukes, Amy Forsyth, Jack Gilpin, Simon Jones, Celia Keenan-Bolger, Ben Lamb, Audra McDonald, Brian Stokes Mitchell, Debra Monk, Hattie Morahan, Donna Murphy, Kristine Nielsen, Kelli O’Hara, Taylor Richardson, Douglas Sills, Erin Wilhelmi, John Douglas Thompson, Taylor Trensch, James Scully, Dennis Haysbert, Maggie Kuntz, Neal Huff, Bonnie Milligan, Jim Gaffigan, Dallas Roberts, Andrew Burnap, Elizabeth Marvel, Adrienne Warren, with Bill Camp and Phylicia Rashad.
	

	Julian Fellowes is the creator, writer and executive producer. Other credits include director and executive producer Salli Richardson-Whitfield; writer and executive producer Sonja Warfield; executive producers Gareth Neame, David Crockett, Bob Greenblatt, Kate Churchill, Davita Scarlett and Elaine Aronson; co-executive producers Erica Armstrong Dunbar and Holly Rymon. HBO and Universal Television, a division of Universal Studio Group, are behind the series.

title: Gavin Newsom Commutes Sentences of All 548 Death Row Inmates in California
description:
Gavin Newsom
                          I Just Commuted Sentences for All Death Row Inmates
body:
Gavin Newsom
                          I Just Commuted Sentences for All Death Row Inmates
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 5, 2026
                            12:27 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Governor Gavin Newsom just commuted the sentences of all 548 prisoners on death row in California in what is one of the largest single-day acts of clemency in U.S. history ... but that doesn't mean they're being freed from prison.
      
    
            Newsom detailed his decision in an open letter Thursday, writing ... "State-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundations of our legal system and diminishes each of us."
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            The governor added ... "I know we cannot execute people in our imperfect legal system and remain true to our core values, first among them justice and human decency."
      

            Newsom said that while many Californians believe that those who commit brutal crimes deserve to die ... he felt as governor that the state cannot morally kill them.
      
    
            He continued ... "I will therefore issue the same commutation to every condemned person -- life without the possibility of parole, the most severe punishment I can lawfully impose and the state of California can ethically enforce. These offenders will die in prison but not by our hands."
      
    
            Former President Joe Biden previously commuted the sentences of roughly 1,500 people in Dec. 2024 ... and Oklahoma voters approved a referendum in Nov. 2019 that released or commuted the sentences for 527 inmates -- with 462 released early.
      
    
            Newsom's commutations come just months after he's set to depart the governorship after completing his second term, with newly elected Dem Xavier Becerra taking over the reins in Jan. 2027.
      
    
            California has not executed a prisoner since Jan. 17, 2006 ... when Clarence Ray Allen was given a lethal injection.
